newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KIDD LEADS FLAMES PAST FLYERS, STARS MOVE TO 5-0.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KIDD LEADS FLAMES PAST FLYERS, STARS MOVE TO 5-0.

text.p: Trevor Kidd made 27 saves for his seventh career shutout and German Titov scored a power-play goal midway through the second period as the Calgary Flames blanked the Philadelphia Flyers 1-0 Sunday.

Kidd made seven saves in each of the first two periods and 13 in the third, but credited his inexperienced defencemen with cramping Philadelphia's imposing squad of forwards, which didn't include injured Eric Lindros and Joel Otto.

"The young (defensemen) are a treat to watch. They are playing like seasoned veterans," said Kidd. "Although Philadelphia has been without Lindros and Otto, they still have a pretty good lineup and (our defence) did not allow them to generate anything."

The Flames generated the game's only goal while Pat Falloon was serving a tripping penalty. Calgary's Cory Stillman took a shot from the right point that goaltender Ron Hextall blocked with his right pad. The puck rebounded to Titov, who shot it into an open net for his second goal.
"It was a good shot. I beat my man to the puck. He did not see me and I got behind him," said Titov. "The rebound came in front to me and I was able to shoot it in the net."
Hextall made 22 saves in a losing cause.
In Chicago, Greg Adams, Benoit Hogue and Grant Marshall scored second-period goals as the Dallas Stars improved to 5-0, the best start in franchise history with a 5-3 victory over the Blackhawks.
Dallas never won more than three straight games last season.

The Hawks were leading 1-0 on Denis Savard's second goal when Adams fired a wrist shot from the slot that beat goaltender Ed Belfour for his fourth of the season to tie the score at 3:04 of the second period.
Dallas took its first lead at 15:19 when Hogue banked a rebound of Pat Verbeek's shot off Belfour's skate.
Just 90 seconds later, Marshall retrieved a loose puck in the left circle and fell backward as he shot the puck, which found its way between Belfour's pads.
In the third period, Dave Reid and Guy Charbonneau added shorthanded goals for Dallas, while Sergei Krivokrasov and Brent Sutter tallied for Chicago.
Andy Moog made 25 saves to post his fourth win.
Belfour made 24 saves and fell to 1-3-0.
